Station inputs, interpolation model and municipal series · Heatwaves, ozone and mortality in Santiago, 2009-2020

Author

Amaru Agüero Jiménez

Published

November 23, 2026

1 What is validated

The ozone exposure of the study is a daily value per municipality, interpolated from the monitoring stations of the SINCA network. Three things can go wrong on the way from the monitors to that value, and each is examined here:

A. The station inputs. Are the station series that feed the interpolation faithful to the measurements? B. The interpolation model. How well do inverse distance weighting (IDW) and ordinary kriging predict ozone at a place without a monitor? C. The municipal series. How much do the delivered series differ from series rebuilt from the measurements, in particular on high-ozone days?

A last section compares the series with an independent source, the CAMS reanalysis, which assimilates satellite ozone retrievals.

The delivered series comes from pollution-interpolation-kriging-idw. Its station inputs are hourly SINCA records trimmed at their 1st and 99th percentiles, averaged over the day when at least 12 hours are valid, and completed by imputation. Its interpolation uses IDW (power 2, at most 5 stations within 15 km) and ordinary kriging with a variogram fitted every day. The validation uses the hourly SINCA records as published, with the validation status of every record, for the 11 ozone stations of the Metropolitan Region.

Code/12_ozone_station_series.R (station series and rebuilt municipal series) 
# 12_ozone_station_series.R
# Ozone at the monitoring stations from the hourly SINCA records, and a
# municipal series rebuilt from them with the data author's interpolation.
#
# Why: the delivered municipal series (script 11) is a 24-hour mean computed
# after trimming the hourly values at their 1st and 99th percentiles and
# filling gaps by imputation. The analysis plan names the daily maximum 8-hour
# mean (MDA8). This script rebuilds both metrics from the hourly records as
# published by SINCA, with no trimming and no imputation, and interpolates
# them with the same model and parameters. Only the hourly records with the
# statuses accepted in the configuration are used.
#
# Inputs
#   inputs$sinca_hourly_dir          hourly ozone by station (ppb)
#   inputs$station_series            station coordinates used by the data author
#   inputs$interpolation_locations   one target point per municipality
# Outputs
#   Data/Derived/ozone_station_daily.csv       station-day: mean24, mda8, valid hours
#   Data/Derived/ozone_rebuilt_municipal.csv   municipality-day: o3obs_* (24-hour
#                                              mean) and o3mda8_* (MDA8)
#   Output/Tables/ozone_station_hourly_status.csv
#   Output/Tables/ozone_rebuilt_qc.csv

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(sp)
  library(gstat)
  library(automap)
})
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))

municipalities <- study_municipalities()
params <- get_param("interpolation")
series_rules <- get_param("station_series")
stopifnot(get_param("air_pollution", "negative_values") == "set_missing")
lag_buffer <- max(unlist(get_param("design", "lags_days")))
keep_dates <- study_dates(buffer_days = lag_buffer)

# ---- 1. Stations and target points ------------------------------------------

station_codes <- fread(here::here(series_rules$stations_file), encoding = "UTF-8")
author <- new.env()
load(input_path("station_series"), envir = author)
load(input_path("interpolation_locations"), envir = author)

station_points <- author$imputed_series[!duplicated(author$imputed_series$station), "station"]
station_points <- merge(station_points, station_codes, by = "station")
stopifnot(nrow(station_points) == nrow(station_codes),
          sf::st_crs(station_points)$epsg == params$crs_epsg)

targets <- author$interpol
stopifnot(setequal(targets$comuna, municipalities$name),
          sf::st_crs(targets)$epsg == params$crs_epsg)

# ---- 2. Daily series by station ---------------------------------------------

read_station <- function(i) {
  file <- file.path(input_path("sinca_hourly_dir"),
                    sprintf(series_rules$hourly_file_pattern, station_codes$sinca_id[i]))
  if (!file.exists(file)) stop("Hourly file not found: ", file, call. = FALSE)
  hourly <- read_sinca_hourly(file, accepted_status = unlist(series_rules$accepted_status))
  daily <- daily_from_hourly(
    hourly,
    min_hours = series_rules$min_valid_hours_day,
    mda8_min_hours = series_rules$mda8_min_hours_window,
    mda8_min_windows = series_rules$mda8_min_windows_day
  )
  status <- hourly[date %in% keep_dates, .(hours = .N), by = status]
  list(
    daily = cbind(station_codes[i], daily[date %in% keep_dates]),
    status = cbind(station_codes[i], status)
  )
}
stations <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(station_codes)), read_station)
station_daily <- rbindlist(lapply(stations, `[[`, "daily"))
hourly_status <- rbindlist(lapply(stations, `[[`, "status"))
hourly_status[is.na(status), status := "no_record"]

setorder(station_daily, station, date)
fwrite(station_daily, file.path(dir_derived, "ozone_station_daily.csv"))
fwrite(dcast(hourly_status, sinca_id + station ~ status, value.var = "hours", fill = 0),
       file.path(dir_tables, "ozone_station_hourly_status.csv"))

# ---- 3. Municipal series rebuilt with the same interpolation ----------------

setkey(station_daily, date)
metric_prefix <- c(mean24 = "o3obs", mda8 = "o3mda8")

rebuild_day <- function(day) {
  out <- data.table(municipality = targets$comuna, date = day)
  for (metric in names(metric_prefix)) {
    prefix <- metric_prefix[[metric]]
    values <- station_daily[.(day)][!is.na(get(metric)), .(station, value = get(metric))]
    out[, (paste0(prefix, "_n_stations")) := nrow(values)]
    if (nrow(values) >= params$ok_min_stations) {
      day_stations <- merge(station_points, values, by = "station")
      result <- with_warnings(interpolate_day(day_stations, targets, "value", params))
      out[, (paste0(prefix, c("_idw", "_ok", "_ok_var"))) := result$value[, .(idw, ok, ok_var)]]
      out[, (paste0(prefix, "_ok_warning")) := length(result$warnings) > 0]
      out[, (paste0(prefix, "_ok_failed")) := !is.na(result$value$ok_error[1])]
    } else {
      out[, (paste0(prefix, c("_idw", "_ok", "_ok_var"))) := NA_real_]
      out[, (paste0(prefix, "_ok_warning")) := NA]
      out[, (paste0(prefix, "_ok_failed")) := NA]
    }
  }
  out
}
# The result does not depend on the number of cores.
rebuilt_days <- parallel::mclapply(as.list(keep_dates), rebuild_day,
                                   mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
failed <- vapply(rebuilt_days, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
if (any(failed)) {
  stop("Interpolation failed on ", format(keep_dates[which(failed)[1]]), ": ",
       rebuilt_days[[which(failed)[1]]], call. = FALSE)
}
rebuilt <- rbindlist(rebuilt_days)
stopifnot(nrow(rebuilt) == nrow(municipalities) * length(keep_dates))

# Same rule as the delivered series for kriging values below zero
qc <- list()
for (prefix in metric_prefix) {
  for (m in c("idw", "ok")) {
    col <- paste0(prefix, "_", m)
    negative <- !is.na(rebuilt[[col]]) & rebuilt[[col]] < 0
    qc[[length(qc) + 1]] <- data.table(
      series = prefix, method = m, rows = nrow(rebuilt),
      missing = sum(is.na(rebuilt[[col]])), negative_set_missing = sum(negative),
      days_below_min_stations = rebuilt[get(paste0(prefix, "_n_stations")) < params$ok_min_stations,
                                        uniqueN(date)],
      days_with_kriging_warning = rebuilt[get(paste0(prefix, "_ok_warning")) == TRUE, uniqueN(date)],
      days_variogram_not_fitted = rebuilt[get(paste0(prefix, "_ok_failed")) == TRUE, uniqueN(date)]
    )
    set(rebuilt, which(negative), col, NA_real_)
    if (m == "ok") set(rebuilt, which(negative), paste0(prefix, "_ok_var"), NA_real_)
  }
}
fwrite(rbindlist(qc), file.path(dir_tables, "ozone_rebuilt_qc.csv"))

rebuilt <- merge(municipalities, rebuilt, by.x = "name", by.y = "municipality")
setnames(rebuilt, c("code", "name"), c("com", "municipality"))
setcolorder(rebuilt, c("com", "municipality", "date"))
setorder(rebuilt, com, date)
fwrite(rebuilt, file.path(dir_derived, "ozone_rebuilt_municipal.csv"))

message("ozone_station_daily.csv: ", nrow(station_daily), " station-days; ",
        "ozone_rebuilt_municipal.csv: ", nrow(rebuilt), " rows")
print(rbindlist(qc))
Code/14_interpolation_validation.R (leave-one-station-out predictions) 
# 14_interpolation_validation.R
# Leave-one-station-out cross-validation of the ozone interpolation.
#
# For every warm-season day of the study years each station is removed in
# turn, the data author's model (IDW and ordinary kriging, same parameters)
# is fitted to the remaining stations, and the removed station is predicted.
# The observed values are the validated 24-hour mean and MDA8 of script 12.
#
# This is the slow step of the pipeline (one variogram fit per day, station
# and metric: about 75 minutes on two cores). It only writes the predictions;
# script 17 turns them into tables.
#
# Inputs
#   Data/Derived/ozone_station_daily.csv   (script 12)
#   inputs$station_series                  station coordinates
# Output
#   Data/Derived/validation_loso_predictions.csv   one row per day, metric and
#                                                  station left out

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(sp)
  library(gstat)
  library(automap)
})
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))

params <- get_param("interpolation")
study_years <- get_param("study", "years")
warm_months <- get_param("study", "warm_season_months")

station_daily <- fread(derived_path("ozone_station_daily.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
station_daily[, date := as.Date(date)]
station_daily <- station_daily[year(date) >= study_years[1] & year(date) <= study_years[2]]
station_daily[, warm_season := is_warm_season(date, warm_months)]

author <- new.env()
load(input_path("station_series"), envir = author)
station_points <- author$imputed_series[!duplicated(author$imputed_series$station), "station"]
station_points <- station_points[station_points$station %in% station_daily$station, ]

cv_days <- sort(unique(station_daily[warm_season == TRUE, date]))
setkey(station_daily, date)

loso_day <- function(day) {
  results <- list()
  for (metric in c("mean24", "mda8")) {
    values <- station_daily[.(day)][!is.na(get(metric)), .(station, value = get(metric))]
    # The fit needs ok_min_stations after one station is removed
    if (nrow(values) - 1 < params$ok_min_stations) next
    points <- merge(station_points, values, by = "station")
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(points))) {
      fit <- with_warnings(interpolate_day(points[-i, ], points[i, ], "value", params))
      results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.table(
        date = day, metric = metric, station = points$station[i],
        observed = points$value[i], n_fit_stations = nrow(points) - 1,
        fit$value, ok_warning = length(fit$warnings) > 0
      )
    }
  }
  rbindlist(results)
}
# The result does not depend on the number of cores.
loso_days <- parallel::mclapply(as.list(cv_days), loso_day, mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
failed <- vapply(loso_days, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
if (any(failed)) {
  stop("Cross-validation failed on ", format(cv_days[which(failed)[1]]), ": ",
       loso_days[[which(failed)[1]]], call. = FALSE)
}
loso <- rbindlist(loso_days)
stopifnot(nrow(loso) > 0)
fwrite(loso, file.path(dir_derived, "validation_loso_predictions.csv"))

message("validation_loso_predictions.csv: ", nrow(loso), " predictions on ", length(cv_days), " days")
Code/17_validation_summary.R (tables of the three validations) 
# 17_validation_summary.R
# Validation of the ozone exposure: tables.
#
# Three questions
#   A. Station inputs: how do the station series used by the data author
#      compare with the daily means computed from the validated hourly SINCA
#      records?
#   B. Interpolation model: how well do IDW and ordinary kriging predict a
#      station left out of the fit (predictions of script 14)?
#   C. Municipal series: how does the delivered series compare with the one
#      rebuilt from the validated records with the same model?
#
# Inputs
#   Data/Derived/ozone_station_daily.csv            (script 12)
#   Data/Derived/exposure_2009_2020.csv             (script 13)
#   Data/Derived/validation_loso_predictions.csv    (script 14)
#   inputs$station_series                           the data author's station series
# Outputs, all in Output/Tables
#   validation_inputs_by_station.csv   validation_inputs_by_level.csv
#   validation_loso_overall.csv        validation_loso_common.csv
#   validation_loso_by_station.csv     validation_loso_high_ozone.csv
#   validation_reproduction.csv        validation_municipal_by_level.csv
#   validation_municipal_flags.csv

source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))

params <- get_param("interpolation")
study_years <- get_param("study", "years")
warm_months <- get_param("study", "warm_season_months")
cutoffs <- unlist(get_param("air_pollution", "ozone_percentile_cutoffs"))
z <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - params$conf_level) / 2)

station_daily <- fread(derived_path("ozone_station_daily.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
station_daily[, date := as.Date(date)]
station_daily <- station_daily[year(date) >= study_years[1] & year(date) <= study_years[2]]

author <- new.env()
load(input_path("station_series"), envir = author)

# ---- A. Station inputs ------------------------------------------------------

author_series <- as.data.table(sf::st_drop_geometry(author$imputed_series))[
  , .(station, date, author_o3 = daily_o3)]
inputs <- merge(station_daily, author_series, by = c("station", "date"), all = TRUE)
inputs <- inputs[!is.na(author_o3) | !is.na(mean24)]
inputs[, warm_season := is_warm_season(date, warm_months)]
inputs[, status := fcase(
  !is.na(author_o3) & is.na(mean24), "no validated daily mean",
  is.na(author_o3) & !is.na(mean24), "observed, absent from the author's series",
  abs(author_o3 - mean24) < 0.005, "identical",
  default = "modified"
)]

inputs_summary <- function(dt) {
  dt[, .(
    station_days = .N,
    identical_pct = 100 * mean(status == "identical"),
    modified_pct = 100 * mean(status == "modified"),
    no_validated_mean_pct = 100 * mean(status == "no validated daily mean"),
    absent_pct = 100 * mean(status == "observed, absent from the author's series"),
    mean_observed = mean(mean24[status %in% c("identical", "modified")]),
    mean_author_same_days = mean(author_o3[status %in% c("identical", "modified")]),
    mean_change_when_modified = mean((author_o3 - mean24)[status == "modified"])
  ), by = station]
}
by_station <- rbind(
  cbind(period = "all days", inputs_summary(inputs)),
  cbind(period = "warm season", inputs_summary(inputs[warm_season == TRUE]))
)
total <- rbind(
  cbind(period = "all days", inputs_summary(copy(inputs)[, station := "All stations"])),
  cbind(period = "warm season",
        inputs_summary(copy(inputs[warm_season == TRUE])[, station := "All stations"]))
)
fwrite(rbind(by_station, total), file.path(dir_tables, "validation_inputs_by_station.csv"))

# Difference by ozone level: warm-season station-days with both values,
# grouped by tenths of the observed 24-hour mean
both <- inputs[warm_season == TRUE & status %in% c("identical", "modified")]
both[, level := cut(mean24, stats::quantile(mean24, 0:10 / 10), include.lowest = TRUE,
                    labels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
by_level <- both[, .(
  station_days = .N, observed_mean24 = mean(mean24), observed_mda8 = mean(mda8, na.rm = TRUE),
  author_mean = mean(author_o3), difference = mean(author_o3 - mean24),
  modified_pct = 100 * mean(status == "modified")
), keyby = level]
fwrite(by_level, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_inputs_by_level.csv"))

# ---- B. Leave-one-station-out cross-validation ------------------------------

loso <- fread(derived_path("validation_loso_predictions.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
loso[, date := as.Date(date)]

loso_long <- melt(loso, id.vars = c("date", "metric", "station", "observed", "ok_var"),
                  measure.vars = c("idw", "ok"), variable.name = "method",
                  value.name = "predicted")
# All station-days that each method could predict
overall <- loso_long[, validation_metrics(observed, predicted), by = .(metric, method)]
# Share of station-days with no prediction (IDW: no station within the search radius)
overall <- merge(overall, loso_long[, .(not_predicted_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(predicted))),
                                    by = .(metric, method)], by = c("metric", "method"))
# Share of observed values inside the nominal kriging interval
coverage <- loso[!is.na(ok), .(method = "ok", interval_coverage_pct =
  100 * mean(abs(observed - ok) <= z * sqrt(ok_var))), by = metric]
overall <- merge(overall, coverage, by = c("metric", "method"), all.x = TRUE)
fwrite(overall, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_loso_overall.csv"))

# The two methods on the same station-days: IDW gives no value when no station
# lies within its search radius, kriging always does, so the sets above differ
common <- loso[!is.na(idw) & !is.na(ok)]
common_long <- melt(common, id.vars = c("date", "metric", "station", "observed"),
                    measure.vars = c("idw", "ok"), variable.name = "method",
                    value.name = "predicted")
fwrite(common_long[, validation_metrics(observed, predicted), by = .(metric, method)],
       file.path(dir_tables, "validation_loso_common.csv"))

by_station_cv <- loso_long[, validation_metrics(observed, predicted),
                           by = .(metric, method, station)]
fwrite(by_station_cv, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_loso_by_station.csv"))

# High-ozone days: observed and predicted values are each classified against
# their own station percentile, as the exposure categories are built
high <- rbindlist(lapply(cutoffs, function(p) {
  d <- loso_long[!is.na(predicted)]
  d[, `:=`(observed_high = as.integer(observed > stats::quantile(observed, p / 100)),
           predicted_high = as.integer(predicted > stats::quantile(predicted, p / 100))),
    by = .(metric, method, station)]
  cbind(percentile = p,
        d[, classification_agreement(observed_high, predicted_high), by = .(metric, method)])
}))
fwrite(high, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_loso_high_ozone.csv"))

# ---- C. Delivered against rebuilt municipal series --------------------------

exposure <- fread(derived_path("exposure_2009_2020.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
exposure[, date := as.Date(date)]
exposure <- exposure[in_study_period == TRUE & warm_season == TRUE]

# Reproduction: on the days when every station value of the author's series
# equals the validated 24-hour mean, the rebuilt municipal series should equal
# the delivered one if this project runs the same interpolation.
day_status <- inputs[, .(all_identical = all(status == "identical")), by = date]
same_input_days <- day_status[all_identical == TRUE, date]
same <- exposure[date %in% same_input_days]
reproduction <- rbindlist(lapply(c("idw", "ok"), function(m) {
  difference <- abs(same[[paste0("o3_", m)]] - same[[paste0("o3obs_", m)]])
  data.table(method = m, days = uniqueN(same$date), municipality_days = sum(!is.na(difference)),
             within_0.001_ppb_pct = 100 * mean(difference < 1e-3, na.rm = TRUE),
             median_abs_difference = stats::median(difference, na.rm = TRUE),
             max_abs_difference = max(difference, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
fwrite(reproduction, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_reproduction.csv"))

municipal_level <- rbindlist(lapply(c("idw", "ok"), function(m) {
  d <- exposure[, .(com, delivered = get(paste0("o3_", m)), rebuilt = get(paste0("o3obs_", m)),
                    mda8 = get(paste0("o3mda8_", m)))]
  d <- d[!is.na(delivered) & !is.na(rebuilt)]
  d[, level := cut(rebuilt, stats::quantile(rebuilt, 0:10 / 10), include.lowest = TRUE,
                   labels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
  cbind(method = m, d[, .(
    municipality_days = .N, rebuilt_mean24 = mean(rebuilt), delivered_mean24 = mean(delivered),
    difference = mean(delivered - rebuilt), rebuilt_mda8 = mean(mda8, na.rm = TRUE)
  ), keyby = level])
}))
fwrite(municipal_level, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_municipal_by_level.csv"))

# Agreement of the high-ozone flags between series (reference: rebuilt)
flag_pairs <- list(c("o3obs", "o3"), c("o3mda8", "o3"), c("o3mda8", "o3obs"))
municipal_flags <- rbindlist(lapply(flag_pairs, function(pair) {
  rbindlist(lapply(c("idw", "ok"), function(m) rbindlist(lapply(cutoffs, function(p) {
    reference <- exposure[[paste0(pair[1], "_", m, "_gt_p", p)]]
    test <- exposure[[paste0(pair[2], "_", m, "_gt_p", p)]]
    values <- exposure[, .(a = get(paste0(pair[1], "_", m)), b = get(paste0(pair[2], "_", m)))]
    cbind(reference = pair[1], compared = pair[2], method = m, percentile = p,
          classification_agreement(reference, test),
          pearson_r = values[!is.na(a) & !is.na(b), cor(a, b)])
  }))))
}))
fwrite(municipal_flags, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_municipal_flags.csv"))

print(overall)
Code/16_reanalysis_comparison.R (comparison with CAMS) 
# 16_reanalysis_comparison.R
# Ozone of the municipal series against the CAMS global reanalysis (EAC4).
#
# CAMS EAC4 assimilates satellite retrievals of ozone into a global chemistry
# model. Its cells measure 0.75 degrees (about 70 by 83 km here), so the whole
# study area falls in two cells: the reanalysis cannot say anything about
# differences between municipalities. It is an independent source for the
# day-to-day course of ozone over the city, which is what this script uses.
#
# Inputs
#   inputs$cams_eac4_dir                    monthly files of 3-hourly values by cell
#   Data/Derived/interpolation_points.csv   (script 15)
#   Data/Derived/exposure_2009_2020.csv     (script 13)
# Outputs
#   Data/Derived/cams_ozone_daily.csv            cell-day: daily mean and afternoon value (ppb)
#   Output/Tables/validation_cams_cells.csv      cells used and municipalities in each
#   Output/Tables/validation_cams_correlation.csv
#
# Correlations are computed for the city-wide daily mean (the mean of the 33
# municipalities), on the warm-season days of the study years, in two forms:
# on the daily values, and on the anomalies from the mean of each calendar
# month, which removes the seasonal cycle shared by any two ozone series.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(ncdf4)
})
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))

rules <- get_param("reanalysis")
study_years <- get_param("study", "years")
warm_months <- get_param("study", "warm_season_months")
# Mass mixing ratio (kg/kg) to volume mixing ratio (ppb): molar masses of dry
# air (28.9644 g/mol) and ozone (47.9982 g/mol)
kgkg_to_ppb <- 28.9644 / 47.9982 * 1e9

# ---- 1. Cells that contain the municipal target points ----------------------

targets <- fread(derived_path("interpolation_points.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
lonlat <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(
  sf::st_as_sf(targets, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = get_param("interpolation", "crs_epsg")), 4326
))
targets[, `:=`(lon = lonlat[, 1], lat = lonlat[, 2])]

files <- list.files(input_path("cams_eac4_dir"), pattern = "\\.nc$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(files) > 0)
first <- ncdf4::nc_open(files[1])
cells <- data.table(pixel = seq_along(ncdf4::ncvar_get(first, "pixel_id")),
                    pixel_id = as.vector(ncdf4::ncvar_get(first, "pixel_id")),
                    cell_lat = as.vector(ncdf4::ncvar_get(first, "latitude")),
                    cell_lon = as.vector(ncdf4::ncvar_get(first, "longitude")))
stopifnot(ncdf4::ncatt_get(first, "o3", "units")$value == "kg kg**-1")
ncdf4::nc_close(first)

half <- rules$cell_size_degrees / 2
targets[, pixel_id := vapply(seq_len(.N), function(i) {
  hit <- cells[abs(cell_lat - lat[i]) <= half & abs(cell_lon - lon[i]) <= half]
  stopifnot(nrow(hit) == 1)
  hit$pixel_id
}, numeric(1))]
used <- cells[pixel_id %in% targets$pixel_id]
fwrite(merge(used[, .(pixel_id, cell_lat, cell_lon)],
             targets[, .(municipalities = .N, names = paste(municipality, collapse = "; ")), by = pixel_id],
             by = "pixel_id"),
       file.path(dir_tables, "validation_cams_cells.csv"))

# ---- 2. Daily values by cell, in local time ---------------------------------

read_month <- function(file) {
  nc <- ncdf4::nc_open(file)
  on.exit(ncdf4::nc_close(nc))
  ids <- as.vector(ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "pixel_id"))
  stopifnot(identical(ids, cells$pixel_id))
  time_units <- ncdf4::ncatt_get(nc, "time", "units")$value
  origin <- as.POSIXct(sub("^[a-z]+ since ", "", time_units), tz = "UTC")
  step <- switch(sub(" since.*$", "", time_units), hours = 3600, seconds = 1, days = 86400)
  stopifnot(!is.null(step))
  utc <- origin + ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "time") * step
  ozone <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "o3")                    # pixel x time
  stopifnot(identical(dim(ozone), c(length(ids), length(utc))))
  rbindlist(lapply(used$pixel, function(p) {
    data.table(pixel_id = ids[p], utc = utc, o3_ppb = ozone[p, ] * kgkg_to_ppb)
  }))
}
cams <- rbindlist(lapply(files, read_month))
stopifnot(anyDuplicated(cams[, .(pixel_id, utc)]) == 0, !anyNA(cams$o3_ppb))
cams[, local := utc + rules$utc_offset_hours * 3600]
cams[, `:=`(date = as.Date(format(local, "%Y-%m-%d", tz = "UTC")),
            hour = as.integer(format(local, "%H", tz = "UTC")))]
afternoon <- unlist(rules$afternoon_local_hours)
stopifnot(all(afternoon %in% unique(cams$hour)))
cams_daily <- cams[, .(
  records = .N,
  cams_mean24 = mean(o3_ppb),
  cams_afternoon = mean(o3_ppb[hour %in% afternoon])
), by = .(pixel_id, date)]
cams_daily <- cams_daily[records == 8]        # complete local days only
fwrite(cams_daily, file.path(dir_derived, "cams_ozone_daily.csv"))

# ---- 3. City-wide daily series and correlations -----------------------------

exposure <- fread(derived_path("exposure_2009_2020.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
exposure[, date := as.Date(date)]
exposure <- exposure[in_study_period == TRUE & warm_season == TRUE]
exposure <- merge(exposure, targets[, .(com, pixel_id)], by = "com")
exposure <- merge(exposure, cams_daily, by = c("pixel_id", "date"))
stopifnot(uniqueN(exposure$date) == uniqueN(cams_daily[
  year(date) >= study_years[1] & year(date) <= study_years[2] & month(date) %in% warm_months, date]))

pairs <- data.table(
  series = c("o3_idw", "o3_ok", "o3obs_idw", "o3obs_ok", "o3mda8_idw", "o3mda8_ok"),
  cams = c(rep("cams_mean24", 4), rep("cams_afternoon", 2))
)
city <- exposure[, c(lapply(.SD, mean, na.rm = TRUE)), by = date,
                 .SDcols = c(pairs$series, "cams_mean24", "cams_afternoon")]
city[, month_id := format(date, "%Y-%m")]
correlations <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) {
  d <- city[, .(date, month_id, x = get(pairs$series[i]), y = get(pairs$cams[i]))][!is.na(x)]
  d[, `:=`(x_anomaly = x - mean(x), y_anomaly = y - mean(y)), by = month_id]
  data.table(series = pairs$series[i], cams = pairs$cams[i], days = nrow(d),
             mean_series = mean(d$x), mean_cams = mean(d$y),
             correlation_daily = cor(d$x, d$y),
             correlation_anomalies = cor(d$x_anomaly, d$y_anomaly))
}))
fwrite(correlations, file.path(dir_tables, "validation_cams_correlation.csv"))
fwrite(city[, !"month_id"], file.path(dir_derived, "cams_city_daily.csv"))
print(correlations)

2 A. Station inputs

The station series published with the interpolation code (2009-2020) are compared, station by station and day by day, with the 24-hour mean computed from the validated hourly records with the same rule of at least 12 valid hours. A station-day is identical when the two values agree, modified when both exist and differ, and has no validated daily mean when the author’s series holds a value that the validated records cannot produce (imputed, or built on records never validated).

Show the code 
kable(by_station[period == "warm season",
                 .(station, station_days, identical_pct, modified_pct, no_validated_mean_pct,
                   mean_observed, mean_author_same_days, mean_change_when_modified)],
      digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Station", "Station-days", "Identical (%)", "Modified (%)",
                    "No validated daily mean (%)", "Observed mean (ppb)",
                    "Author's mean, same days (ppb)", "Mean change when modified (ppb)"))

In the warm season 16.0% of the station-days were modified and 6.5% have no validated daily mean. The modifications are not spread evenly: they concentrate on the days with most ozone.

Show the code 
level_long <- melt(by_level[, .(level, `Observed` = observed_mean24, `Author's series` = author_mean)],
                   id.vars = "level", variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
level_long[, level := factor(level, levels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
ggplot(level_long, aes(level, ozone, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Observed" = "#2a78d6", "Author's series" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "Tenth of the observed 24-hour mean (D1 lowest, D10 highest)",
       y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL)
Show the code 
kable(by_level, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Tenth", "Station-days", "Observed 24-hour mean (ppb)", "Observed MDA8 (ppb)",
                    "Author's mean (ppb)", "Difference (ppb)", "Modified (%)"))

On the tenth of station-days with most ozone the author’s series is 6.5 ppb lower than the measurements (25.1 against 31.6 ppb, a 20% reduction), and 78% of those station-days were modified. This is what trimming the hourly values at their 99th percentile does to ozone: the hours it removes are the afternoon peaks of the hottest days, so the daily mean of exactly those days is pulled down. The trimming flattens the upper tail of the exposure that the study is about.

Show the code 
both <- inputs[warm_season == TRUE & !is.na(author_o3) & !is.na(mean24)]
ggplot(both, aes(mean24, author_o3)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 80) +
  geom_abline(colour = ink$primary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_magnitude(name = "Station-days", trans = "log10") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Observed 24-hour mean (ppb)", y = "Author's series (ppb)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.justification = "center")

2.1 Records that were never validated

SINCA marks every hourly record as validated, preliminary or not validated. Most records of the study period are validated, but some station-periods were never validated, and one of them is an evident instrument failure.

Show the code 
rules <- get_param("station_series")
codes <- fread(here::here(rules$stations_file), encoding = "UTF-8")
any_status <- daily_from_hourly(
  read_sinca_hourly(file.path(input_path("sinca_hourly_dir"),
                              sprintf(rules$hourly_file_pattern, codes[station == "Independencia", sinca_id])),
                    accepted_status = c("validated", "preliminary", "not_validated")),
  min_hours = rules$min_valid_hours_day, mda8_min_hours = rules$mda8_min_hours_window,
  mda8_min_windows = rules$mda8_min_windows_day
)[, .(date, any_status = mean24)]
window <- merge(inputs[date >= as.Date("2015-01-01") & date <= as.Date("2017-12-31")],
                any_status, by = "date", all.x = TRUE)
window[, month_start := as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01"))]
monthly <- window[, .(
  `Independencia, records of any status` = mean(any_status[station == "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  `Independencia, author's series` = mean(author_o3[station == "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  `Other stations, author's series` = mean(author_o3[station != "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  validated_days = sum(station == "Independencia" & !is.na(mean24))
), by = month_start]
shade <- monthly[validated_days == 0, .(xmin = month_start, xmax = month_start + 31)]
monthly_long <- melt(monthly, id.vars = "month_start", measure.vars = 2:4,
                     variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
no_validated <- inputs[station == "Independencia" & year(date) == 2016 & is.na(mean24) & !is.na(author_o3), .N]
ggplot(monthly_long) +
  geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = ink$grid, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(month_start, ozone, colour = series), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Independencia, records of any status" = "#1baf7a",
                                 "Independencia, author's series" = "#eb6834",
                                 "Other stations, author's series" = ink$muted)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3))

From February 2016 the hourly records of the Independencia monitor fall far below every other station and none of them was ever validated. The author’s series does not follow them: for the 328 days of 2016 without a validated daily mean it holds imputed values, so that for most of that year the station enters the interpolation as an estimate and not as a measurement. The series rebuilt here use validated records only (accepted_status in the configuration) and leave a station out of the days for which it has none, at the cost of about 3% of the warm-season station-days.

3 B. The interpolation model

Leave-one-station-out cross-validation: for every warm-season day of 2009-2020 each station is removed in turn, the model is fitted to the remaining stations with the author’s function and parameters, and the removed station is predicted. The observed values are the validated 24-hour mean and MDA8.

Show the code 
loso_table <- copy(loso)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(loso_table[, .(metric, method, n, mean_observed, bias, mae, rmse, nrmse_pct, pearson_r, r2,
                     not_predicted_pct, interval_coverage_pct)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 1), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Method", "Station-days", "Observed mean (ppb)", "Bias (ppb)",
                    "MAE (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)", "RMSE (% of mean)", "Pearson r", "R²",
                    "Not predicted (%)", "Inside the 95% kriging interval (%)"))

IDW gives no value when no station lies within its 15 km radius, which is always the case for Talagante and sometimes for other stations when their neighbours have no validated record; kriging always gives one. The table above therefore compares the methods on different station-days. On the station-days that both methods predict:

3.1 High-ozone days

The analysis classifies days as high ozone against a percentile of each place. The same is done here with the predictions: a station-day is predicted high when the prediction exceeds the percentile of the predictions at that station.

Show the code 
high_table <- copy(loso_high)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(high_table[order(metric, percentile, method),
                 .(metric, percentile = paste0("> P", percentile), method, n,
                   sensitivity = 100 * sensitivity, specificity = 100 * specificity,
                   agreement = 100 * agreement, kappa)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Cut-off", "Method", "Station-days", "Sensitivity (%)",
                    "Specificity (%)", "Agreement (%)", "Kappa"))

4 C. Delivered and rebuilt municipal series

Script 12 interpolates the validated station values to the 33 municipalities with the same model: o3obs is the 24-hour mean and o3mda8 the daily maximum 8-hour mean.

First, a reproduction test. On the days when every station value of the author’s series equals the validated 24-hour mean, the two municipal series have the same inputs and should coincide if this project runs the same interpolation.

Show the code 
reproduction <- read_table("validation_reproduction.csv")
kable(reproduction[, .(method = method_label[method], days, municipality_days, within_0.001_ppb_pct,
                       median_abs_difference, max_abs_difference)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 6, 4), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Method", "Days", "Municipality-days", "Within 0.001 ppb (%)",
                    "Median absolute difference (ppb)", "Largest absolute difference (ppb)"))

With the same inputs this project returns the delivered values: all of the IDW values and nearly all of the kriging values agree to the third decimal (the daily variogram fit makes kriging sensitive to the last digits of its inputs). The differences shown in the rest of this section therefore come from the station inputs.

Show the code

                               `Rebuilt from validated records` = rebuilt_mean24,
                               `Delivered` = delivered_mean24)],
           id.vars = c("method", "level"), variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")

ggplot(ml, aes(level, ozone, colour = series, group = series)) +

5 An independent source: the CAMS reanalysis

No satellite measures ozone at the surface with the resolution of a city: the ozone column seen from space is dominated by the stratosphere. The closest independent source is a reanalysis that assimilates the satellite retrievals into a chemistry model. CAMS EAC4 has cells of 0.75 degrees, so the 33 municipalities fall in two cells and the comparison says nothing about differences between municipalities. What it can check is whether the day-to-day course of ozone over the city in the station-based series is also seen by a source that does not use the monitors.

Show the code 
cams_series <- c(o3_idw = "Delivered 24-hour mean, IDW", o3_ok = "Delivered 24-hour mean, kriging",
                 o3obs_idw = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean, IDW", o3obs_ok = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean, kriging",
                 o3mda8_idw = "Rebuilt MDA8, IDW", o3mda8_ok = "Rebuilt MDA8, kriging")
cams_table <- copy(cams)[, `:=`(series = cams_series[series],
                                cams = fifelse(cams == "cams_mean24", "Daily mean", "Afternoon (15 and 18 h)"))]
kable(cams_table, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Station-based series", "CAMS value", "Days", "Series mean (ppb)",
                    "CAMS mean (ppb)", "Correlation, daily values", "Correlation, anomalies"))

CAMS is a weak reference for surface ozone in a basin that one of its cells covers almost entirely, mountains included: its values are much higher than the monitors and the correlations are modest. Within those limits, the series rebuilt from validated records follow it more closely than the delivered series, and the MDA8 more closely than the 24-hour mean.

6 What this means for the analysis

Show the code 
common_wide <- dcast(loso_common, metric ~ method, value.var = c("rmse", "r2"))
mda8_flags <- municipal_flags[reference == "o3mda8" & compared == "o3" & method == "idw"]
coverage <- loso[method == "ok", .(metric, interval_coverage_pct)]
las_condes <- loso_station[station == "Las Condes" & metric == "mda8" & method == "ok"]
top_municipal <- municipal_level[method == "idw" & level == "D10"]
  1. The delivered series understates the days with most ozone. Its station inputs are 6.5 ppb below the measurements on the highest tenth of station-days, and its municipal values are 3.6 ppb below the rebuilt ones on the highest tenth of municipality-days. A study of high-ozone days and of their interaction with heat should not use inputs trimmed at the 99th percentile.
  2. Station-days without a validated measurement are estimates. In the delivered series 6.5% of the warm-season station-days have no validated daily mean; the Independencia monitor, which failed in 2016, is carried by imputed values for most of that year. The rebuilt series use validated records only.
  3. The metric matters. The plan names the MDA8; the delivered series is a 24-hour mean. Among the municipality-days above the 75th percentile of MDA8, the delivered 24-hour mean flags 67% as high ozone (kappa 0.56).
  4. Interpolation method. On the same station-days ordinary kriging has the lower cross-validation error for both metrics: RMSE 4.00 against 4.61 ppb for the 24-hour mean and 7.35 against 7.59 ppb for the MDA8. The difference is clear for the 24-hour mean and small for the MDA8. The kriging intervals contain the left-out observation 75% of the time for the MDA8 and 84% of the time for the 24-hour mean, against a nominal 95%, so they should not be read as measurement uncertainty. The working value of the configuration is still IDW; this result argues for kriging and the choice is open.
  5. What interpolation cannot fix. Nine to eleven monitors describe 33 municipalities, and the error is far from uniform. Las Condes, the station with most ozone, cannot be predicted from the others (bias -13.3 ppb when it is left out): the eastern municipalities depend on that single monitor. The cross-validation error is the error at a monitored site when its own monitor is ignored; it is the best available estimate of the error in municipalities without a monitor, not a guarantee.

The exposure dataset keeps the three series (o3, o3obs, o3mda8) so that the choice can be made by the principal investigator and its effect shown as a sensitivity analysis. The working value in the configuration is still the delivered series.

---
title: "Validation of the ozone exposure"
subtitle: "Station inputs, interpolation model and municipal series · Heatwaves, ozone and mortality in Santiago, 2009-2020"
author: "Amaru Agüero Jiménez"
date: today
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "01_functions.R"))
source(here::here("Code", "02_plot_style.R"))
library(knitr)
theme_set(theme_report())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
study_years <- get_param("study", "years")
warm_months <- get_param("study", "warm_season_months")

station_daily <- fread(derived_path("ozone_station_daily.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
station_daily[, date := as.Date(date)]
author <- new.env()
load(input_path("station_series"), envir = author)
author_series <- as.data.table(sf::st_drop_geometry(author$imputed_series))[
  , .(station, date, author_o3 = daily_o3)]
inputs <- merge(station_daily, author_series, by = c("station", "date"), all = TRUE)
inputs <- inputs[year(date) >= study_years[1] & year(date) <= study_years[2]]
inputs[, warm_season := is_warm_season(date, warm_months)]

by_station <- read_table("validation_inputs_by_station.csv")
by_level <- read_table("validation_inputs_by_level.csv")
loso <- read_table("validation_loso_overall.csv")
loso_common <- read_table("validation_loso_common.csv")
loso_station <- read_table("validation_loso_by_station.csv")
loso_high <- read_table("validation_loso_high_ozone.csv")
municipal_level <- read_table("validation_municipal_by_level.csv")
municipal_flags <- read_table("validation_municipal_flags.csv")
cams <- read_table("validation_cams_correlation.csv")

metric_label <- c(mean24 = "24-hour mean", mda8 = "MDA8")
method_label <- c(idw = "IDW", ok = "Ordinary kriging")
all_warm <- by_station[period == "warm season" & station == "All stations"]
top <- by_level[level == "D10"]
```

## What is validated

The ozone exposure of the study is a daily value per municipality, interpolated
from the monitoring stations of the SINCA network. Three things can go wrong on
the way from the monitors to that value, and each is examined here:

A. **The station inputs.** Are the station series that feed the interpolation
   faithful to the measurements?
B. **The interpolation model.** How well do inverse distance weighting (IDW)
   and ordinary kriging predict ozone at a place without a monitor?
C. **The municipal series.** How much do the delivered series differ from
   series rebuilt from the measurements, in particular on high-ozone days?

A last section compares the series with an independent source, the CAMS
reanalysis, which assimilates satellite ozone retrievals.

The delivered series comes from `pollution-interpolation-kriging-idw`. Its
station inputs are hourly SINCA records trimmed at their 1st and 99th
percentiles, averaged over the day when at least 12 hours are valid, and
completed by imputation. Its interpolation uses IDW (power 2, at most 5
stations within 15 km) and ordinary kriging with a variogram fitted every day.
The validation uses the hourly SINCA records as published, with the validation
status of every record, for the 11 ozone stations of the Metropolitan Region.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| file: ../Code/12_ozone_station_series.R
#| code-summary: "Code/12_ozone_station_series.R (station series and rebuilt municipal series)"
```

```{r}

#| file: ../Code/14_interpolation_validation.R
#| code-summary: "Code/14_interpolation_validation.R (leave-one-station-out predictions)"
```


## A. Station inputs

The station series published with the interpolation code (2009-2020) are
compared, station by station and day by day, with the 24-hour mean computed
from the validated hourly records with the same rule of at least 12 valid
hours. A station-day is *identical* when the two values agree, *modified* when
both exist and differ, and has *no validated daily mean* when the author's
series holds a value that the validated records cannot produce (imputed, or
built on records never validated).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inputs
#| tbl-cap: "Author's station series against the validated hourly records, warm seasons 2009-2020."
kable(by_station[period == "warm season",
                 .(station, station_days, identical_pct, modified_pct, no_validated_mean_pct,
                   mean_observed, mean_author_same_days, mean_change_when_modified)],
      digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Station", "Station-days", "Identical (%)", "Modified (%)",
                    "No validated daily mean (%)", "Observed mean (ppb)",
                    "Author's mean, same days (ppb)", "Mean change when modified (ppb)"))
```

In the warm season `r fmt(all_warm$modified_pct)`% of the station-days were
modified and `r fmt(all_warm$no_validated_mean_pct)`% have no validated daily
mean. The modifications are not spread evenly: they concentrate on the days
with most ozone.

```{r}
#| label: fig-level
#| fig-cap: "Author's station series against the observed 24-hour mean, by tenths of the observed value. Warm-season station-days with both values."
#| fig-height: 3.8
level_long <- melt(by_level[, .(level, `Observed` = observed_mean24, `Author's series` = author_mean)],
                   id.vars = "level", variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
level_long[, level := factor(level, levels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
ggplot(level_long, aes(level, ozone, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Observed" = "#2a78d6", "Author's series" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "Tenth of the observed 24-hour mean (D1 lowest, D10 highest)",
       y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-level
#| tbl-cap: "Values behind the figure, with the observed MDA8 of the same days and the share of modified station-days."
kable(by_level, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Tenth", "Station-days", "Observed 24-hour mean (ppb)", "Observed MDA8 (ppb)",
                    "Author's mean (ppb)", "Difference (ppb)", "Modified (%)"))
```

On the tenth of station-days with most ozone the author's series is
`r fmt(abs(top$difference))` ppb lower than the measurements
(`r fmt(top$author_mean)` against `r fmt(top$observed_mean24)` ppb, a
`r fmt(100 * abs(top$difference) / top$observed_mean24, 0)`% reduction), and
`r fmt(top$modified_pct, 0)`% of those station-days were modified. This is what
trimming the hourly values at their 99th percentile does to ozone: the hours it
removes are the afternoon peaks of the hottest days, so the daily mean of
exactly those days is pulled down. The trimming flattens the upper tail of the
exposure that the study is about.

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Author's station series against the observed 24-hour mean, warm-season station-days 2009-2020. The line is equality."
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-width: 5.4
both <- inputs[warm_season == TRUE & !is.na(author_o3) & !is.na(mean24)]
ggplot(both, aes(mean24, author_o3)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 80) +
  geom_abline(colour = ink$primary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_magnitude(name = "Station-days", trans = "log10") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Observed 24-hour mean (ppb)", y = "Author's series (ppb)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.justification = "center")
```

### Records that were never validated

SINCA marks every hourly record as validated, preliminary or not validated.
Most records of the study period are validated, but some station-periods were
never validated, and one of them is an evident instrument failure.

```{r}
#| label: fig-independencia
#| fig-cap: "Independencia, 2015-2017, monthly mean of the 24-hour ozone: hourly records of any status, the author's series, and the mean of the other stations in the author's series. Shaded: months in which Independencia has no validated record."
#| fig-height: 3.8
rules <- get_param("station_series")
codes <- fread(here::here(rules$stations_file), encoding = "UTF-8")
any_status <- daily_from_hourly(
  read_sinca_hourly(file.path(input_path("sinca_hourly_dir"),
                              sprintf(rules$hourly_file_pattern, codes[station == "Independencia", sinca_id])),
                    accepted_status = c("validated", "preliminary", "not_validated")),
  min_hours = rules$min_valid_hours_day, mda8_min_hours = rules$mda8_min_hours_window,
  mda8_min_windows = rules$mda8_min_windows_day
)[, .(date, any_status = mean24)]
window <- merge(inputs[date >= as.Date("2015-01-01") & date <= as.Date("2017-12-31")],
                any_status, by = "date", all.x = TRUE)
window[, month_start := as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01"))]
monthly <- window[, .(
  `Independencia, records of any status` = mean(any_status[station == "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  `Independencia, author's series` = mean(author_o3[station == "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  `Other stations, author's series` = mean(author_o3[station != "Independencia"], na.rm = TRUE),
  validated_days = sum(station == "Independencia" & !is.na(mean24))
), by = month_start]
shade <- monthly[validated_days == 0, .(xmin = month_start, xmax = month_start + 31)]
monthly_long <- melt(monthly, id.vars = "month_start", measure.vars = 2:4,
                     variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
no_validated <- inputs[station == "Independencia" & year(date) == 2016 & is.na(mean24) & !is.na(author_o3), .N]
ggplot(monthly_long) +
  geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = ink$grid, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(month_start, ozone, colour = series), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Independencia, records of any status" = "#1baf7a",
                                 "Independencia, author's series" = "#eb6834",
                                 "Other stations, author's series" = ink$muted)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3))
```

From February 2016 the hourly records of the Independencia monitor fall far
below every other station and none of them was ever validated. The author's
series does not follow them: for the `r no_validated` days of 2016 without a
validated daily mean it holds imputed values, so that for most of that year
the station enters the interpolation as an estimate and not as a measurement.
The series rebuilt here use validated records only (`accepted_status` in the
configuration) and leave a station out of the days for which it has none, at
the cost of about 3% of the warm-season station-days.

## B. The interpolation model

Leave-one-station-out cross-validation: for every warm-season day of 2009-2020
each station is removed in turn, the model is fitted to the remaining stations
with the author's function and parameters, and the removed station is
predicted. The observed values are the validated 24-hour mean and MDA8.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso
#| tbl-cap: "Leave-one-station-out cross-validation, warm seasons 2009-2020. R² is the coefficient of determination against the 1:1 line."
loso_table <- copy(loso)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(loso_table[, .(metric, method, n, mean_observed, bias, mae, rmse, nrmse_pct, pearson_r, r2,
                     not_predicted_pct, interval_coverage_pct)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 1), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Method", "Station-days", "Observed mean (ppb)", "Bias (ppb)",
                    "MAE (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)", "RMSE (% of mean)", "Pearson r", "R²",
                    "Not predicted (%)", "Inside the 95% kriging interval (%)"))
```

IDW gives no value when no station lies within its 15 km radius, which is
always the case for Talagante and sometimes for other stations when their
neighbours have no validated record; kriging always gives one. The table above
therefore compares the methods on different station-days. On the station-days
that both methods predict:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso-common
#| tbl-cap: "The two methods on the same station-days."
common_table <- copy(loso_common)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(common_table[order(metric, method), .(metric, method, n, bias, mae, rmse, nrmse_pct, pearson_r, r2)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Method", "Station-days", "Bias (ppb)", "MAE (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)",
                    "RMSE (% of mean)", "Pearson r", "R²"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-loso-station
#| fig-cap: "Cross-validation error by station: RMSE as a percentage of the station mean."
#| fig-height: 4.6
station_plot <- copy(loso_station)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
order_station <- station_plot[metric == "MDA8" & method == "IDW"][order(nrmse_pct), station]
ggplot(station_plot, aes(nrmse_pct, factor(station, levels = order_station), colour = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colour_method) +
  labs(x = "RMSE (% of the station mean)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso-station
#| tbl-cap: "Cross-validation by station."
kableExtra::scroll_box(
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    kable(station_plot[order(metric, station, method),
                       .(metric, station, method, n, mean_observed, bias, rmse, pearson_r, r2)],
          format = "html", digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
          col.names = c("Metric", "Station", "Method", "Station-days", "Observed mean (ppb)",
                        "Bias (ppb)", "RMSE (ppb)", "Pearson r", "R²")),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12),
  height = "380px"
)
```

### High-ozone days

The analysis classifies days as high ozone against a percentile of each place.
The same is done here with the predictions: a station-day is predicted high
when the prediction exceeds the percentile of the predictions at that station.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loso-high
#| tbl-cap: "High-ozone days: predicted against observed classification at the station left out."
high_table <- copy(loso_high)[, `:=`(metric = metric_label[metric], method = method_label[method])]
kable(high_table[order(metric, percentile, method),
                 .(metric, percentile = paste0("> P", percentile), method, n,
                   sensitivity = 100 * sensitivity, specificity = 100 * specificity,
                   agreement = 100 * agreement, kappa)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Metric", "Cut-off", "Method", "Station-days", "Sensitivity (%)",
                    "Specificity (%)", "Agreement (%)", "Kappa"))
```

## C. Delivered and rebuilt municipal series

Script 12 interpolates the validated station values to the 33 municipalities
with the same model: `o3obs` is the 24-hour mean and `o3mda8` the daily maximum
8-hour mean.

First, a reproduction test. On the days when every station value of the
author's series equals the validated 24-hour mean, the two municipal series
have the same inputs and should coincide if this project runs the same
interpolation.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reproduction
#| tbl-cap: "Rebuilt against delivered municipal ozone on the warm-season days with identical station inputs."
reproduction <- read_table("validation_reproduction.csv")
kable(reproduction[, .(method = method_label[method], days, municipality_days, within_0.001_ppb_pct,
                       median_abs_difference, max_abs_difference)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 6, 4), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Method", "Days", "Municipality-days", "Within 0.001 ppb (%)",
                    "Median absolute difference (ppb)", "Largest absolute difference (ppb)"))
```

With the same inputs this project returns the delivered values: all of the IDW
values and nearly all of the kriging values agree to the third decimal (the
daily variogram fit makes kriging sensitive to the last digits of its inputs).
The differences shown in the rest of this section therefore come from the
station inputs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-municipal-level
#| fig-cap: "Delivered against rebuilt 24-hour mean by tenths of the rebuilt value, municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020."
#| fig-height: 3.8
ml <- melt(municipal_level[, .(method = method_label[method], level,
                               `Rebuilt from validated records` = rebuilt_mean24,
                               `Delivered` = delivered_mean24)],
           id.vars = c("method", "level"), variable.name = "series", value.name = "ozone")
ml[, level := factor(level, levels = paste0("D", 1:10))]
ggplot(ml, aes(level, ozone, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~method) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Rebuilt from validated records" = "#2a78d6", "Delivered" = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(x = "Tenth of the rebuilt 24-hour mean (D1 lowest, D10 highest)",
       y = "Ozone, 24-hour mean (ppb)", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-municipal-level
#| tbl-cap: "Values behind the figure, with the rebuilt MDA8 of the same municipality-days."
kable(municipal_level[, .(method = method_label[method], level, municipality_days, rebuilt_mean24,
                          delivered_mean24, difference, rebuilt_mda8)],
      digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Method", "Tenth", "Municipality-days", "Rebuilt 24-hour mean (ppb)",
                    "Delivered (ppb)", "Difference (ppb)", "Rebuilt MDA8 (ppb)"))
```

### Does the choice of series change who is exposed?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flags
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement of the high-ozone flags between series, municipality-days of the warm seasons 2009-2020. Sensitivity and specificity take the first series as reference."
series_label <- c(o3 = "Delivered 24-hour mean", o3obs = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean", o3mda8 = "Rebuilt MDA8")
flags <- copy(municipal_flags)[, `:=`(reference = series_label[reference], compared = series_label[compared],
                                      method = method_label[method])]
kable(flags[, .(reference, compared, method, percentile = paste0("> P", percentile), pearson_r,
                sensitivity = 100 * sensitivity, specificity = 100 * specificity,
                agreement = 100 * agreement, kappa)],
      digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2),
      col.names = c("Reference", "Compared", "Method", "Cut-off", "Pearson r", "Sensitivity (%)",
                    "Specificity (%)", "Agreement (%)", "Kappa"))
```

## An independent source: the CAMS reanalysis

No satellite measures ozone at the surface with the resolution of a city: the
ozone column seen from space is dominated by the stratosphere. The closest
independent source is a reanalysis that assimilates the satellite retrievals
into a chemistry model. CAMS EAC4 has cells of 0.75 degrees, so the 33
municipalities fall in two cells and the comparison says nothing about
differences between municipalities. What it can check is whether the
day-to-day course of ozone over the city in the station-based series is also
seen by a source that does not use the monitors.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cams
#| tbl-cap: "City-wide daily ozone against CAMS EAC4, warm seasons 2009-2020. Anomalies are deviations from the mean of each calendar month."
cams_series <- c(o3_idw = "Delivered 24-hour mean, IDW", o3_ok = "Delivered 24-hour mean, kriging",
                 o3obs_idw = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean, IDW", o3obs_ok = "Rebuilt 24-hour mean, kriging",
                 o3mda8_idw = "Rebuilt MDA8, IDW", o3mda8_ok = "Rebuilt MDA8, kriging")
cams_table <- copy(cams)[, `:=`(series = cams_series[series],
                                cams = fifelse(cams == "cams_mean24", "Daily mean", "Afternoon (15 and 18 h)"))]
kable(cams_table, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      col.names = c("Station-based series", "CAMS value", "Days", "Series mean (ppb)",
                    "CAMS mean (ppb)", "Correlation, daily values", "Correlation, anomalies"))
```

CAMS is a weak reference for surface ozone in a basin that one of its cells
covers almost entirely, mountains included: its values are much higher than
the monitors and the correlations are modest. Within those limits, the series
rebuilt from validated records follow it more closely than the delivered
series, and the MDA8 more closely than the 24-hour mean.

## What this means for the analysis

```{r}
#| label: conclusions
common_wide <- dcast(loso_common, metric ~ method, value.var = c("rmse", "r2"))
mda8_flags <- municipal_flags[reference == "o3mda8" & compared == "o3" & method == "idw"]
coverage <- loso[method == "ok", .(metric, interval_coverage_pct)]
las_condes <- loso_station[station == "Las Condes" & metric == "mda8" & method == "ok"]
top_municipal <- municipal_level[method == "idw" & level == "D10"]
```

1. **The delivered series understates the days with most ozone.** Its station
   inputs are `r fmt(abs(top$difference))` ppb below the measurements on the
   highest tenth of station-days, and its municipal values are
   `r fmt(abs(top_municipal$difference))` ppb below the rebuilt ones on the
   highest tenth of municipality-days. A study of high-ozone days and of their
   interaction with heat should not use inputs trimmed at the 99th percentile.
2. **Station-days without a validated measurement are estimates.** In the
   delivered series `r fmt(all_warm$no_validated_mean_pct)`% of the warm-season
   station-days have no validated daily mean; the Independencia monitor, which
   failed in 2016, is carried by imputed values for most of that year. The
   rebuilt series use validated records only.
3. **The metric matters.** The plan names the MDA8; the delivered series is a
   24-hour mean. Among the municipality-days above the 75th percentile of
   MDA8, the delivered 24-hour mean flags
   `r fmt(100 * mda8_flags[percentile == 75, sensitivity], 0)`% as high ozone
   (kappa `r fmt(mda8_flags[percentile == 75, kappa], 2)`).
4. **Interpolation method.** On the same station-days ordinary kriging has
   the lower cross-validation error for both metrics: RMSE
   `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mean24", rmse_ok], 2)` against
   `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mean24", rmse_idw], 2)` ppb for the 24-hour
   mean and `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mda8", rmse_ok], 2)` against
   `r fmt(common_wide[metric == "mda8", rmse_idw], 2)` ppb for the MDA8. The
   difference is clear for the 24-hour mean and small for the MDA8. The kriging
   intervals contain the left-out observation
   `r paste(sprintf("%s%% of the time for the %s", fmt(coverage$interval_coverage_pct, 0), metric_label[coverage$metric]), collapse = " and ")`,
   against a nominal 95%, so they should not be read as measurement
   uncertainty. The working value of the configuration is still IDW; this
   result argues for kriging and the choice is open.
5. **What interpolation cannot fix.** Nine to eleven monitors describe 33
   municipalities, and the error is far from uniform. Las Condes, the station
   with most ozone, cannot be predicted from the others (bias
   `r fmt(las_condes$bias)` ppb when it is left out): the eastern
   municipalities depend on that single monitor. The cross-validation error is
   the error at a monitored site when its own monitor is ignored; it is the
   best available estimate of the error in municipalities without a monitor,
   not a guarantee.

The exposure dataset keeps the three series (`o3`, `o3obs`, `o3mda8`) so that
the choice can be made by the principal investigator and its effect shown as a
sensitivity analysis. The working value in the configuration is still the
delivered series.

```{r}
#| label: session
#| code-summary: "Session information"
sessionInfo()
```
